headline: Energy Surges as Tech Buckles; Geopolitical Sparks Light the Week Ahead
body_html:
Friday's session closed on a decidedly defensive note. Of 544 stocks in our universe, just 160 finished higher while 381 fell, as selling pressure concentrated in technology. Semiconductors shed 3.76% as a group, with Software off 2.14%, dragging the broader tape lower. Vicor Corporation plunged 12.92%, Twilio dropped 10.62%, and Okta slid 10.20%, while Ichor Holdings, MaxLinear, and Snowflake each lost between 8% and 10% — a punishing sweep across chips, cloud identity, and data infrastructure.

The lone bright spot was Energy, which rose 1.73% on the day and stood well clear of every other sector. Range Resources, EOG Resources, and Chord Energy each gained more than 4%, while Tenaris, Canadian Natural Resources, and EQT Corp posted advances between 3.5% and 3.75%. The catalyst was hard to miss: Iranian Revolutionary Guards reported two tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, a separate vessel was hit by an unknown projectile off Saudi Arabia, and Egypt's president moved to seek parliamentary authority to defend the kingdom if called upon.

Traders walk into Monday, October 19 with Middle East risk premiums freshly repriced. The Iranian parliament's confirmation of a new defence minister, active U.S. diplomatic shuttling across Central Asia, and Lebanon's military delegation pressing Washington for a ceasefire all suggest the geopolitical backdrop will remain a primary market driver. Energy names sensitive to supply-route disruption and haven assets warrant close attention at the open.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Mines and a Struck Tanker Jolt Oil Markets
briefs.body: Iranian Revolutionary Guards reported two tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, while a separate vessel was struck by an unknown projectile off Saudi Arabia the same day. The back-to-back incidents in critical shipping corridors sent energy stocks sharply higher and kept crude risk premiums elevated heading into the new week.

briefs.headline: Iran Installs New Defence Chief as Regional Tensions Simmer
briefs.body: Iran's parliament formally approved Mehrdad Akhlaqi as the country's new minister of defence, a transition that analysts say could signal a shift in how Tehran manages its military posture. The appointment lands as Iranian-linked incidents in the Strait of Hormuz draw renewed international scrutiny.

briefs.headline: Egypt Moves to Authorise Saudi Defence Commitment
briefs.body: President Sisi has taken the unusual step of seeking Egyptian parliament's approval to deploy forces in defence of Saudi Arabia if requested. The move reflects the widening circle of states preparing contingency positions as tensions across the Gulf and broader Middle East intensify.

briefs.headline: Apple Reports Extraordinary Demand for New iPhone Duo
briefs.body: Apple said demand for its latest iPhone Duo has been extraordinary, with delivery delays already emerging. The disclosure points to robust consumer appetite heading into the holiday quarter, offering a rare piece of constructive news for consumer-technology sentiment even as software and semiconductor stocks suffered on Friday.

briefs.headline: Snowflake, Twilio, and Okta Lead Software Selloff
briefs.body: The software sector dropped 2.14% on Friday, with Snowflake falling 8.43%, Twilio losing 10.62%, and Okta sliding 10.20%. The broad-based retreat across cloud data, communications platforms, and identity security suggests institutional investors are reducing exposure to growth-oriented software ahead of a potentially volatile earnings season.

briefs.headline: Jio's Multibillion-Dollar IPO Puts Ambani Brand to the Test
briefs.body: Reliance's Jio unit launched a roughly $3.2 billion initial public offering aimed squarely at India's young, mobile-first consumer base. The listing is being watched as a gauge of how much appetite remains for large-cap emerging-market technology offerings at a moment when global risk sentiment is under pressure.
